rules.sentence: Atypical variants are more prone to recur and as a result, re-excision might be necessary.
Although the clinical diagnosis of DFs may be simple in daily practice, in the presence of various patterns, diagnosis of DFs can become challenging.
Therefore, specific characterization of these atypical variants is essential in differentiating them from malignant conditions and assessing the risk of local recurrence.

DFs usually have an excellent prognosis and do not require treatment unless the lesion is changing, bleeding, becomes symptomatic or suspicious, another diagnosis is more probable or the patient demands it clinical cosmetic reasons.
Complete surgical excision with clear margins for histopathologic examination is the most common therapy.
